extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and evaluating rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 and 103 (anticipation, public use/sale, inventorship, foreign patenting, obviousness, and related 103(c)/common-ownership issues) during USPTO examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(e), Copending Application with Common Assignee or Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by [2]. The applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application. Based upon the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the reference, it constitutes prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph is used to reject over a patent or patent application publication with an earlier filing date that discloses the claimed invention. The patent or publication must have either a common assignee or a common inventor. This rejection might be overcome either by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the reference was derived from the inventor of this application and is thus not the invention 'by another,' or by an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131. This form paragraph must be preceded by either of form paragraphs 7.12 or 7.12.01. If the claims of the copending application conflict with the claims of the instant application, a provisional double patenting rejection should also be given using form paragraphs 8.30 and 8.32. If evidence shows either invention is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or (g), use form paragraphs 7.13 and/or 7.14. In bracket 3, insert either '--assignee--' or '--inventor--'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(e), No Common Assignee or Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being [2] by [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph is used to reject over a patent or patent application publication with an earlier filing date that discloses but does not claim the same invention. The patent or publication must have neither a common assignee nor a common inventor. In bracket 2, insert either '--clearly anticipated--' or '--anticipated--' with an explanation at the end of the paragraph. In bracket 3, insert the prior art relied upon. Patent application publications may only be used if this form paragraph was preceded by form paragraph 7.12.01. Patent application publications may only be used if this form paragraph was preceded by form paragraph 7.12.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(b) Public Use or On Sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) based upon a public use or sale of the invention. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded either by form paragraphs 7.07 and 7.09 or by form paragraph 7.103. A full explanation of the evidence establishing a public use or sale must be provided in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(c) Abandonment of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded either by form paragraph 7.07 and 7.10 or by form paragraph 7.103. In bracket 2, insert a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment of the invention. See MPEP § 2134.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(d) Foreign Patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as being barred by applicants [2]. [3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded either by form paragraphs 7.07 and 7.11 or by form paragraph 7.103. In bracket 3, insert an explanation of this rejection which must include appropriate dates and how they make the foreign patent available under 35 U.S.C. 102(d). Refer to MPEP § 2135 for applicable 35 U.S.C. 102(d) prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(f) Applicant Not the Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) because the applicant did not invent the claimed subject matter. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded either by paragraphs 7.07 and 7.13 or by paragraph 7.103. In bracket 2, insert an explanation of the supporting evidence establishing that applicant was not the inventor. See MPEP § 2137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of a 35 U.S.C. 103 Rejection (A–D)
rubrics_metrics.description: After indicating that the rejection is under 35 U.S.C. 103, the examiner should set forth in the Office action: (A) the relevant teachings of the prior art relied upon, (B) the difference(s) in the claim over the applied reference(s), (C) the proposed modification of the applied reference(s) necessary to arrive at the claimed subject matter, and (D) an explanation why one of ordinary skill in the art at the time the invention was made would have been motivated to make the proposed modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide relevant teachings preferably with column/page/line citations. Explain differences between claim and references, the needed modification(s), and why a person of ordinary skill would be motivated to make those modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie case of obviousness: three basic criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish a prima facie case of obviousness, three basic criteria must be met: (1) there must be some suggestion or motivation, either in the references themselves or in the knowledge generally available to one of ordinary skill in the art, to modify the reference or to combine reference teachings; (2) there must be a reasonable expectation of success; and (3) the prior art reference(s) must teach or suggest all the claim limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The teaching or suggestion to make the claimed combination and the reasonable expectation of success must both be found in the prior art and not based on applicant’s disclosure. See In re Vaeck and MPEP § 2143–§ 2143.03 for decisions pertinent to these criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner burden: provide suggestion/motivation or convincing line of reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial burden is on the examiner to provide some suggestion of the desirability of doing what the inventor has done — either the references must expressly or impliedly suggest the claimed invention or the examiner must present a convincing line of reasoning why the artisan would have found the claimed invention obvious in light of the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A convincing line of reasoning is required where the suggestion is not explicit in the prior art. See Ex parte Clapp and MPEP § 2144–§ 2144.09 for examples of reasoning supporting obviousness rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference inclusion: include any relied-on reference positively in the rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reference is relied on to support a rejection, whether or not in a minor capacity, that reference should be positively included in the statement of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the reference explicitly in the rejection statement (see In re Hoch). Properly identify each relied-on reference so the applicant can clearly identify the issues and respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection (obviousness) under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103: application and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rejections of the obviousness type under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 are rejections applied to copending applications having different effective filing dates wherein each application has a common assignee or a common inventor. The earlier filed application, if patented, would constitute prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective November 29, 1999, subject matter that was prior art under former 103 via 102(e) is disqualified if the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned at the time the invention was made (see 35 U.S.C. 103(c)). A provisional rejection alerts the applicant and gives opportunity to avoid loss of rights. Confidential status of applications under 35 U.S.C. 122 must be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to overcome a provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 rejection (A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 can be overcome by: (A) arguing patentability over the earlier filed application; (B) combining the subject matter of the copending applications into a single application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and abandoning the copending applications; (C) filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 showing unclaimed invention disclosed in copending application was derived from the inventor of the other application; (D) filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 showing a date of invention prior to the effective U.S. filing date of the copending application; or (E) for an application filed on or after November 29, 1999, showing that the prior art and the claimed invention were, at the time the invention was made, owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: combining applications to claim 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit requires that the earlier application contain a disclosure complying with 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph for each claim; a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(c) may be used where appropriate if the earlier application has matured into a patent. See MPEP for details and judicial decisions (Studiengesellschaft Kohle, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103(c) disqualification of prior art (common ownership exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 103(c), subject matter developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under subsections (e), (f), and (g) of 35 U.S.C. 102 shall not preclude patentability where the subject matter and the claimed invention were, at the time the invention was made, owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 103(c) applies only to obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103 and does not affect subject matter that qualifies as anticipatory prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102. The burden of establishing disqualification under 103(c) lies on the person urging it (e.g., applicant). For applications filed on or after November 29, 1999, 102(e) prior art may be disqualified under amended 103(c); pre-November 29, 1999 rules are more limited. See MPEP §§ 706.02(l) and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'commonly owned' for 35 U.S.C. 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'commonly owned' means wholly (100%) owned by the same person(s) or organization(s) at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either the subject matter or the claimed invention is owned less than 100% by the same entities, common ownership does not exist. For joint ventures, both the application and the reference must have been owned by or subject to assignment to the joint venture at the time the invention was made. A mere license where basic ownership rights are retained does not defeat ownership. Ownership must be actual/enforceable at the relevant time; moral or unenforceable obligations do not suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing common ownership: burden, evidence and examiner assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of establishing that subject matter is disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) rests on the person urging disqualification (e.g., the applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement such as 'Application X and Patent Z were, at the time the invention of Application X was made, jointly owned by Companies A and B' would be sufficient evidence of common ownership. The examiner must examine the application as to all grounds except 102(e),(f),(g) as they apply through 103 only if the application file(s) establishes common ownership at the time the later invention was made. Applicants have an obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor/invention dates and lack of common ownership to enable the examiner to consider appropriate rejections. The examiner will assume compliance unless evidence to the contrary is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for claiming 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit (inventorship and disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application claiming the benefit of a prior filed copending national or international application under 35 U.S.C. 120 must name as an inventor at least one inventor named in the prior filed application. The prior filed application must also disclose the named inventor's invention claimed in at least one claim of the later filed application in the manner provided by the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: So long as the applications have at least one inventor in common and the other requirements are met, the Office will permit a claim for 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit without additional submissions from applicants regarding inventorship differences. In addition to normal examination, the examiner must examine the earlier filed application to determine if the earlier and later applications have at least one inventor in common and that the other 35 U.S.C. 120 requirements are met. The claim for 120 benefit will be permitted without examination of the earlier application for disclosure and support of at least one claim of the later-filed application under 35 U.S.C. 112 unless it becomes necessary to do so (for example, because of an intervening reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting rejections and terminal disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claims of copending applications conflict, a provisional double patenting rejection should be given. Non-statutory and statutory double patenting rejections, based on subject matter disqualified as prior art under amended 35 U.S.C. 103(c), should still be made as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double patenting rejections can be overcome by terminal disclaimers (see 37 CFR 1.321(c)). The practice of rejecting claims in commonly owned applications of different inventive entities on the grounds of double patenting has been reinstituted in appropriate circumstances to prevent improper extension of patent protection while permitting legitimate benefits to inventors/assignees. See In re Bowers and MPEP § 804 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of 35 U.S.C. 103(c) amendment and related procedural points
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective November 29, 1999, subject matter which was prior art under former 35 U.S.C. 103 via 35 U.S.C. 102(e) is disqualified as prior art against the claimed invention if that subject matter and the claimed invention were, at the time the invention was made, owned by the same person or subject to obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change applies to all utility, design and plant patent applications filed on or after November 29, 1999, including continuing applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), continued prosecution applications under 37 CFR 1.53(d), and reissues. It does not affect applications filed before November 29, 1999 or certain requests for examination/continued examination. The mere filing of a continuing application on or after Nov 29, 1999 with required evidence of common ownership will serve to exclude commonly owned 102(e) prior art that was applied in the parent. For reissue applications, the recapture doctrine may prevent presentation of claims that were canceled/amended to overcome 102(e)/103 prior art applied in the application which matured into the patent for which reissue is sought.
